items.hook: Published June 1 by GMO Flatt Security researcher RyotaK: a single malicious GitHub Issue could compromise any repository using the official Claude Code GitHub Actions workflow — including Anthropic's own repos. Root cause: `checkWritePermissions` unconditionally trusted any actor ending in `[bot]`, regardless of actual permissions, allowing an attacker with a GitHub App installation token (free, implicit read access to any public repo) to inject code into the action and propagate it downstream. Patched in Claude Code GitHub Actions v1.0.94. If your repo uses any version before v1.0.94, audit immediately. Anthropic issued remediation guidance alongside the disclosure.

items.name: Microsoft Security: Claude Code GitHub Action Leaks CI/CD Secrets via Prompt Injection
items.hook: Published June 5 by Microsoft Threat Intelligence. The Claude Code GitHub Action's Read tool was not sandboxed the same way as subprocess execution — specifically, it was authorized to access `/proc/self/environ`, meaning a prompt-injection payload in an untrusted PR description, issue body, or comment could instruct Claude to read and exfiltrate `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and other workflow secrets. Anthropic patched this in v2.1.128 by blocking sensitive `/proc` file reads. The mitigation is now live. Microsoft's hardening guidance introduces the 'Agents Rule of Two': never let an AI workflow simultaneously (1) process untrusted input, (2) hold secrets or sensitive access, and (3) communicate externally or change state — any two is manageable, all three is a breach vector. If your org runs Claude Code GitHub Actions and hasn't updated since v2.1.128, update immediately.

items.name: Mitiga Labs: 5-Step MCP Attack Steals OAuth Tokens — Anthropic Declines to Patch
items.hook: Mitiga Labs published the full chain on May 8; Security Boulevard added the remediation framing on June 10. The attack: (1) victim installs a malicious npm package; (2) a postinstall lifecycle hook executes silently; (3) it modifies `~/.claude.json` — the global config governing how Claude Code routes all MCP traffic and stores OAuth tokens in plaintext; (4) MCP traffic is redirected through an attacker-controlled proxy; (5) bearer tokens for Jira, Confluence, and GitHub are intercepted. The tokens are persistent (stored refresh tokens), broadly scoped (all permissions from authorization time), weakly stored (plaintext in `~/.claude.json`), and indistinguishable server-side from legitimate Anthropic egress. Mitiga reported to Anthropic April 10; on April 12 Anthropic said it was out of scope ('user prior consent'). No patch planned. Security Boulevard's June 10 framing: the fix must come from agent containment (per-state tool restrictions, domain allowlists, MCP server validation) not from patching the config file. Immediate actions: monitor `~/.claude.json` for unexpected URL changes, audit npm packages with postinstall hooks, rotate OAuth tokens.

items.name: Claude Code v2.1.172 — Sub-Agents Can Now Spawn Sub-Agents (5 Levels Deep)
items.hook: For most of 2026, 'subagents cannot spawn other subagents' was a deliberate Claude Code guardrail against infinite recursion. v2.1.172 (June 10) lifted it: sub-agents can now spawn their own sub-agents up to 5 levels deep. The purpose is context isolation, not parallelization — each sub-agent gets a fresh 200K-token window, so a deeply nested workflow offloads its noisy work without polluting the parent's context. Foreground sub-agents can spawn at any depth level; background sub-agents at level 5 cannot go further. Token cost: roughly 7× per branch, so practical use is 2–3 levels.
